chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: 'Trees' and Lois Deppe and Orlando Roberson
summary: Hughes asks about songs she did; Lois Deppe's claim about singing the song first and the idea of the style.

blocks.x: that just about winds it up as far as Pittsburgh is concerned, except I would like to ask you one more thing. That is, you mentioned a couple of songs early on during these interviews which you sang, you mentioned Brown Bird Singing and Trees.
Yeah, well Trees was a very popular song that I did. There had been a version of it by Orlando Robeson with one of the bands.
With Claude Hopkins.
Claude Hopkins yes, and so . .
He sang almost like a count to ten, didn't he?

Yes, very high. And of course 'Trees' was very popular at the time and it was one of my specialties when I was at the club. In fact it was the specialty if, you know, if you sing a lot of songs. Just like 'Loch Lomond' now. But I in fact was doing 'Trees' at the Onux Club. You know when I went into Loew's State with the Columbia Band under the direction of Lea Stevens, they put on Loew's State stage, they presented Saturday Night Swing Club.
This is in New York?

New York City. Yeah, this was later on. And I had 'Trees' in my repertoire and I was going to do it, but the manager came back after the first show and said, you can't sing 'Trees' because you got, 'only God could make a tree' in it and you couldn't use the word 'God' on the stage at the time. I don't know. You can do a lot of things that we couldn't do back in 1938 and '37. But I had to take 'Trees' our of my repertoire and that was my big number. And of course, Bob Burk singing, 'It's Another One of Those Songs'.
Oh, by the way just before we get onto that I was also reading in the book Earl Hines today that Lois Deppe makes the claim that he was the first person to sing 'Trees' on the radio.
I wouldn't be a bit surprised.
And he sang that with Don Redman.
Yes, I wouldn't be a bit surprised.
You never heard that?
I never heard it. Probably Orlando Robeson got the idea to do it, or the band, and

have Orlando sing it.
Did Lois Deppe sing in a similar kind of style to Orlando?

No, I think the song I remember having heard Lois Step sing on a record was 'Sometimes I Feel Like a Motherless Child'. In fact, that's the only vocal I heard because the other side of the other record was strictly instrumental and he didn't sing on it. But I remember his vocal as 'Sometimes I Feel Like A Motherless Child'. And I think that in the production "Great Day" he sang "Hallelujah". Well, in 1948 in Pittsburgh at the Syria Mosque they had a night of stars and they had four generations beginning with Lois Sdeppa, Earl Hines, Billy Eckstine, and Erroll Garner. Erroll Garner had just become popular at the time.
Yes.

And so the general idea was that Lois SHeppc had started this and then Billye, Earl had worked for us, and Billye had appeared with Earl Hines and Erroll Garner with Billye Eckstine, and of course they all had become fullness in their own right.
